top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, single credited writer) best meets the common criteria on the evidence the committee has. As publicly described, Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid show an unmistakable voice, with dense, recursive prose that turns memory, the body and dream into a metaphysical structure. The project looks like one cumulative undertaking across verse and prose rather than a single peak, and the attribution is clean: one writer, one language. The citation I support rests on the prose and names poetry only as its root, because translated coverage of the poetry is thinner. It makes no claim of lineage, completeness or a lifetime's work. The main reservations stay open. Sentence-level achievement in Romanian can be judged only through translation and critical report. Digressive maximalism may be excess rather than depth. Nobody has shown which later volumes extend rather than repeat the earlier project. The inward mode may limit breadth of significance. I have not read the originals or independently verified sources. These uncertainties do not justify no award, since P000 would discard the only proposal that all six files support on literary grounds. I therefore rank P000 second.
